title: Render manifest — The Weekly Drop, indoor-TV correction

blender.reason: No Blender output appears in the locked cut. Every picture is photographic and every product surface is drawn in Remotion, so the CG plate queue is not reduced — it is empty. The Weekly Drop revision did not change this.

obsoletedQueue.disposition: Left in place as the R&D film's record and NOT run. Section 21 of the brief is explicit that obsolete shots must not be rendered; these plates belong to shots the photographic cut does not contain. Running them would have cost ~14.9 CPU hours and produced nothing that could appear in the film.
obsoletedQueue.whatWouldRevivIt: Only a creative decision to put a CG shot back in the cut. The scripts, caches, sharding, determinism fixes and render-worker-bootstrap.sh are untouched and would still work.

remotion.note: One local Remotion worker, 1,344 frames. No Blender or render fleet. Only network wording and acquisition pictures changed; all timing is preserved.

derivedArtifacts.note: Every delivered file except the master and the teaser is a deterministic transform of the master, so a re-render cannot leave a stale artifact behind.

reproducibilitySafeguardsPreserved: Deterministic hashing and the fixed PYTHONHASHSEED behaviour in the Blender window-light code are untouched.
Exact frame ranges are declared per shot in final-edit.json and enforced by preflight; no frame-count relabelling.
Pixel-based still equivalence rather than PNG byte hashing remains the rule in the existing review scripts.
Checksums are recorded for every collected source picture and every delivered artifact.
All asset paths in the edit are repository-relative under public/.
The film's grain is a pure function of the frame number, so two renders of the same commit agree.

compositing.surface: Normal landscape wall-mounted TV inside Main Street Car Wash waiting room
compositing.method: 1600x900 Remotion offer projected by homography into the measured still-space TV quad. Coordinates scale to the native 1928x1076 locked-camera motion source. Three-pixel inset preserves the black bezel.
compositing.why: The TV is ordinary indoor business hardware. Exact offer typography is controlled in compositing, while the generated customer lifts his head to notice it.
compositing.checked: Source bounds, landscape placement, plate identity, screen area/bezel and uninterrupted source motion; wide and close still tests plus motion/composite review.

execution.audio: Existing unchanged Remotion soundtrack embedded during the master/teaser renders; existing final-deliver loudness normalization applied.

tools.localWrappers: /private/tmp/uptick-tv-bin (PATH); ffprobe wrapper sets DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH to the Remotion compositor directory.

execution.portableRebuild: npm run film:final with ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH and FILM_CHROME set to an installed Chromium executable.
execution.webmRestart: The initial cpu-used=2 WebM encode was intentionally stopped for excessive local encode time. Only WebM was restarted via encode_webm(MASTER) at cpu-used=4, preserving CRF 32 and 1080p; the complete new file is validated before delivery.
execution.contactCleanup: Removed the four older sheet1–4.png derivatives. final-deliver.py now clears that legacy naming scheme and rebuilds final-sheet1–4.png.
